# A Real Appendix

`\giEnableAppendix`, fired at the end of the previous chapter,
switches numbering from "Chapter 4" to "Appendix A" — automatically,
with no manual bookkeeping. Notice this chapter's own title has no
"Appendix A:" baked into it; that label is generated for you, the
same way "Chapter N" was for every earlier chapter. Writing "Appendix
A:" directly into the title text here would produce a redundant,
doubled-up label instead.

```{=latex}
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.3\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.6\linewidth}
@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\rowcolor{giTableHeaderShade}
\textbf{Term} & \textbf{Definition} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}Appendix & A back-matter chapter that's lettered instead of numbered. \\
\bottomrule
\caption{\label{tbl-appendix-example}A table inside a real, lettered appendix.}
\end{longtable}
```

A book can have several appendices — just add more `.qmd` files to
`chapters:` after this one; each gets the next letter automatically
(Appendix B, Appendix C, ...).

```{=latex}
% \backmatter fires a \clearpage of its own, so — same lesson as
% \mainmatter/\giEnableMainMatter earlier — it needs to execute
% BEFORE the next chapter's heading, not after. This file is the
% last appendix before back matter, so this switch lives at its
% true end rather than at the top of references.qmd.
\giEnableBackMatter
```
